findings.summary: The single-source 'oq-resolution' rule names only the `**Resolution:**` marker. The old developer.md hard rule 8 also banned `RESOLVED:` and `✅ RESOLVED`. The 'pre-work' rule (line 79) also lost two clauses: 'references an RFC with unresolved OQs' and 'do not file follow-up tasks or dispatch subagents'. CLAUDE.md, which every session still loads, keeps the full marker list and the scope-creep rule. The reviewer gate and the CI DoR upstream-OQ gate do not change. So this narrows advisory prompt text only; no enforced control is weakened. Suggest restoring the three marker spellings and the RFC-OQ clause to the rule text.

findings.summary: The 'force-push' rule says 'any push to `main`/`master` [is] blocked by the PreToolUse hook'. lease-push-guard.js / enforce-blocked-actions.js refuse FORCE pushes to protected branches, but they do not appear to refuse a plain fast-forward `git push origin HEAD:main`. GitHub branch protection is the real backstop there. The old prompts stated 'Never push to main or master' as a behavioural rule; the new text presents it as hook-enforced, which overclaims the control. Suggest rewording to 'never push to main/master (force pushes are hook-blocked; branch protection blocks the rest)'.
